Can You Finance Land in Colorado?

Yes — but it’s not the same as financing a house. Land loans in Colorado come with unique rules, higher down payments, and lender requirements that catch many buyers off guard. Here’s what you should know before applying.

What Makes Land Loans Different?

Land loans carry more risk for lenders, especially when there are no improvements (like a well, driveway, or electric access). As a result, the terms can be more strict.

  • Most land loans require 15%–50% down
  • Shorter loan terms (10–20 years)
  • Higher interest rates than traditional mortgages
Tip: A property with a well, driveway, electric, and septic may qualify for better terms than raw land.

USDA Loan Options (0% Down)

If you’re buying land with a home already on it, you may qualify for a USDA Rural Development loan. These loans offer:

  • Zero down payment
  • Low interest rates
  • Available in designated rural areas

Check USDA Eligibility Map

What Lenders Look For

Each lender is different, but here are a few things they’ll typically evaluate:

  • Land access (year-round road and legal easement)
  • Utility availability (power, well, septic)
  • Zoning and buildability

Want more help? Contact a land-specialized lender early in your search so you're ready when the right parcel pops up.
